rules.intent: Read-only file or symbol lookup, locating tests, tracing a bounded call path, or a straightforward factual query. Return concise evidence, not implementation or design decisions.
Read-only discovery across many files: map modules and dependencies, gather references in an unfamiliar repository, or inspect images. Gather evidence rather than make hard technical decisions.
General-purpose nontrivial implementation or debugging involving state, multiple interfaces, unclear causes, or interacting files. Reliable working code matters more than minimizing cost.
Substantive implementation or behavior-preserving refactoring with clear requirements, requesting a fresh independent approach or an alternative to an earlier implementation.
Tool-heavy implementation and integration: coordinate shell commands, builds, tests, and repairs to deliver a working change. The main challenge is executing and checking the terminal workflow.
A bounded feature or bug fix with explicit requirements and a known approach. Implement a focused patch economically without difficult architecture or root-cause analysis.
Routine test implementation, standard validation logic, repetitive but precise code changes, or conventional implementation patterns with clear expected results.
A small straightforward script, configuration edit, rename, or mechanical one-location change requiring little analysis. Optimize for low cost.
A self-contained coding helper with explicit inputs and outputs where low token and cache cost matter more than latency. No high-risk design, difficult debugging, or final review.
Default technical judgment: analyze code, diagnose bugs, compare tradeoffs, plan changes, or review correctness and requirements. Ordinary design and review belong here, without premium escalation.
Write, translate, summarize, or organize prose using supplied evidence. General text synthesis without difficult code reasoning, high-risk technical decisions, or final correctness/security sign-off.
An explicitly independent technical perspective, adversarial critique, alternative root-cause hypothesis, or comparison of competing approaches after an earlier analysis.
Reconcile a detailed design, requirements, interfaces, and a plan, or synthesize an architectural explanation from extensive evidence. Structured consistency checking without exceptional risk.
Exceptional risk or unresolved difficulty: subtle security/concurrency flaws, dangerous migrations, conflicting invariants, or failed serious prior analyses. Not routine design, review, or prose.
Unusually difficult formal, mathematical, or algorithmic reasoning requiring a derivation or proof, or explicit escalation after standard reasoning failed. Not routine planning or review.
